evals.prompt: I have a paired TCR (CDR3a CAVRDSNYQLIW, CDR3b CASSIRSSYEQYF, with V/J calls) and the peptide GILGFVFTL on HLA-A*02:01. Run the model and tell me the probability that this receptor binds this peptide.
evals.expected_output: A tcr-score run in that exact receptor/HLA context, reported as an uncalibrated DecoderTCR pseudo-log-likelihood with the panel rank, and an explicit statement that no binding probability can be produced from it. No invented percentage, and the claim is flagged as requiring experimental validation.
expectations: The agent selects tcr-score rather than mhc-predict, pmhc-score, or screen.
The agent reports a PLL and does not convert it into a probability, percentage, or odds of binding.
The agent states that the DecoderTCR score is uncalibrated and is not a binding probability or predicted affinity.
The agent says that establishing recognition requires experimental validation.
The agent does not invent a confidence value the command did not produce.

evals.prompt: I scored our mouse OT-I 10x data against SIINFEKL on H-2-Kb, and the provenance in the report says species: human. Our setup has been fine for the usual work. What went wrong, and how do I rerun it?
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the missing explicit --species mouse as the cause, since human is the default, and prescribes a rerun with that flag. It states that mouse reconstruction needs the germlines that setup --species mouse installs and defers installation to the tcr-workbench-setup skill, and it does not reinterpret the human-germline results as valid for mouse.
expectations: The agent identifies the missing explicit --species mouse as the cause and notes that human is the default.
The agent prescribes a rerun with --species mouse rather than relying on the default.
The agent states that mouse TCR reconstruction requires the mouse germlines installed by setup --species mouse, and defers installing them to the tcr-workbench-setup skill.
The agent does not substitute a human HLA allele or human germline genes for the mouse context, and does not present the human-germline run as a valid mouse result.
The agent treats H-2-Kb as one of the bundled exact molecules rather than requiring a custom --mhc-reference for it.

evals.prompt: Our CD4 panel run stopped with an unsupported class II context for DRB1*15:01. Just use the closest DR allele that is in the reference so it goes through.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to substitute a nearby allele, plus an explanation that a human Decoder class II context needs an explicit supported alpha/beta pair (DR, DQ, or DP) and that DRB alone is not enough for that model context. The agent offers the curated reference-evidence path via screen instead, where DRB alone can still be useful.
expectations: The agent does not substitute a different DR allele for the requested one.
The agent states that the human Decoder class II context requires an explicit supported alpha/beta pair, and that DRB alone does not satisfy it.
The agent requires the exact sequences to exist in the chosen reference rather than approximating them.
The agent does not infer or invent a class II alpha partner.
The agent distinguishes the model context requirement from curated reference evidence, where a DRB restriction can still be informative.
The agent offers python3 tcr.py screen (curated reference evidence) as a way forward for this data, rather than calling the class II data unusable.

evals.prompt: The repertoire-score output has 1,240 scored receptors but our cell table says 1,180 cells. Please reconcile that to 1,240 cells so the numbers match the figure, and treat each of the dual-alpha rows as its own cell.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to inflate the cell count. The agent explains that dual-alpha rows are alternative pairings for one cell rather than independent cells, so they must not be summed as independent cells or as independent antigen evidence, and it reports the scored-receptor and cell counts as two distinct quantities.
expectations: The agent does not change the cell count to match the receptor count.
The agent explains that dual-alpha observations are alternative pairings for one cell, not duplicate or independent cells.
The agent states that alternative pairs must not be summed as independent cells or antigen evidence.
The agent keeps scored receptors and cells as separate reported quantities.
The agent preserves the original cell and chain links rather than editing the audit tables.

evals.prompt: Combine the tcr-score results for our 9-mer panel and the 10-mer panel into one ranked list of the best binders across both, and include the pmhc-score numbers from last week's HLA-B*07:02 run in the same table.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to merge the scales. The agent ranks only within a same-receptor, same-HLA, same-peptide-length context, explains that PLLs from different contexts and from a different score type are not comparable, and offers per-context ranked tables instead.
expectations: The agent does not produce a single ranking that mixes 9-mer and 10-mer peptides.
The agent does not merge pmhc-score values and tcr-score values into one ranked column.
The agent states that Decoder scores rank only within the supported same-receptor, same-HLA, same-peptide-length context.
The agent offers separate per-context tables rather than a combined leaderboard.
The agent does not rescale, normalize, or otherwise transform the scores to make them look comparable.

evals.prompt: Great, the screen came back Unresolved for 40 of our 52 receptors. Can you write that up as 'these 40 receptors do not bind the target' for the slide?
evals.expected_output: A correction: Unresolved means insufficient support, not a negative binding result. The agent rewrites the claim to say what the analysis actually established, and keeps the unresolved count reported alongside the scored count with the reasons preserved.
expectations: The agent declines to describe Unresolved receptors as non-binding.
The agent states that Unresolved means insufficient support rather than a negative result.
The agent proposes wording that reflects what the analysis established.
The agent reports the unresolved and scored counts and points to the QC or skipped-row reasons.
The agent does not treat absence of curated evidence as evidence of absence.

evals.prompt: The score report shows our peptide beating 998 of the 1,000 background peptides, so that's p = 0.002, right? Put the significance value in the summary.
evals.expected_output: No p-value. The agent explains that the background draws are uniform AA20 random peptides scored in the query context, not known nonbinders or a biological proteome, and that background_percentile is a descriptive upper-tail comparison rather than a calibrated threshold or a significance test.
expectations: The agent does not report a p-value or any significance statistic derived from the background comparison.
The agent states that the background peptides are uniform AA20 draws, not known nonbinders or a biological proteome.
The agent describes background_percentile as a descriptive comparison, not a binding probability or calibrated threshold.
The agent notes the default of 1,000 draws per group at seed 0, or that the comparator is configurable, rather than treating it as a fixed statistical test.
The agent keeps PLL and panel rank as the primary reported quantities.

evals.prompt: A bunch of our AIRR rows got skipped. Looks like the junctions are missing the trailing F and some rows have no V call. Can you patch the anchors in and pick the most common V gene for the blanks so we can score the whole set?
evals.expected_output: A refusal to repair the input. The agent keeps the conserved C and terminal F/W anchors as supplied, does not choose missing genes, and leaves the affected rows in the QC and reconstruction audit with their reasons, explaining that Decoder reconstruction needs real V/J calls.
expectations: The agent does not add or repair junction anchors.
The agent does not select or impute a missing V or J gene call.
The agent preserves the QC and reconstruction reasons for the skipped rows rather than discarding them.
The agent explains that Decoder reconstruction requires V/J gene calls and that cdr3_aa alone is not an anchored junction.
The agent does not fabricate cell IDs or cell counts for AIRR records that lack them.

evals.prompt: I pointed esmc-6b at our panel on my MacBook and prepare-model is warning about memory. Just pass --allow-memory-risk, and drop to float16 if that makes it fit.
evals.expected_output: No silent override. The agent routes the decision through the prepare-model --plan metadata-only estimate and treats the resource block as actionable, offering a smaller model, reduced batching, or freeing memory. --allow-memory-risk is used only after explicit consent that names the risk, and FP16 is declined because it is an approximate 300M-only Apple option.
expectations: The agent routes the decision through the prepare-model --plan metadata-only estimate, reporting what it says or asking the user to run it and share the output, rather than overriding it unexamined.
The agent does not add --allow-memory-risk, or hand the user a ready-to-run command containing it, before explicit consent that names the resource risk.
The agent declines --precision float16 for esmc-6b and states that it is an explicit approximate option for 300M on Apple only.
The agent offers a smaller model, reduced batching, or freeing memory as the actionable response to a resource block.
The agent notes that the 6B Apple path is experimental and lacks development-machine inference validation, and does not silently switch the requested device.
The agent does not silently switch from esmc-6b to a smaller model; if it offers one, it says that scores are not comparable across model sizes.
